newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANI writes down Holter assets.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANI writes down Holter assets.

text.p: Australian National Industries Ltd (ANI) said on Tuesday it had written down the value of the assets of its troubled German environmental engineering unit Holter by A$234 million in its 1995/96 balance sheet.

ANI said that while the company continues its due dilligence and negotiations for a merger of the environmental business of German government-owned Saarbergwerke AG and Holter, other possibilities were being actively pursued for the merger or joint venturing of the Holter businesses.

ANI said it has written off all of Holter's A$149.3 million goodwill and written down the values of plant and equipment by A$72.3 million and the value of investments in joint ventures by A$12.0 million.

"The board believes that, painful as these decisions may be, they are necessary and in the long term interests of shareholders to enable future maximum value to be extracted from Holter's assets and, in turn, to place the ANI group in a position to provide the growth of shareholder wealth which the baord and management are confident will be produced by the strong core metals and engineering businesses of the ANI group."
ANI announced in November last year that it planned a merger between Holter and Saarberg, with Saarberg replacing Kruger, a Danish company, as ANI's partner in the Kruger Holter waste joint venture.
ANI said on Tuesday that the Holter businesses had been a continuing source of disappointment and had failed to meet its targeted objectives.

"It returned extremely disappointing results in the half year to June 30, 1996, in which there were cost over-runs, technical difficulties and further delays associated with commissioning of waste-to-energy plants," ANI said.
It said this situation was exacerbated in the period by a deterioration in environmental engineering markets generally.

ANI said a number of steps had been taken to address the difficulties faced by Holter including an independent review which confirmed that Holter needed a strong complementary partner in order to be successful.
As well, cost reductions of about 20 percent were being implemented and senior management changes and an organisational restructure had been implemented.
ANI's environmental engineering business reported a A$55.17 million operating loss in the year to June 30, 1996 compared with a loss of A$4.47 million in 1994/95.
